title: Large algebraically closed extensions make arbitrary schemes Jacobson
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $U$ any scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme]. There exists an algebraically closed field extension $K/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension] such that $U_K=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has both properties: (i) for every closed subset $Z$ of the underlying topological space of $U_K$, the closed points of $U_K$ lying in $Z$ are dense in $Z$; (ii) for every closed point $u$ of $U_K$, the structure map $K\to\kappa(u)$ is an isomorphism. Closed points and residue fields are [def-weil-closed-points, def-weil-residue-field]. There is no finite-type, quasi-compactness, reducedness or separatedness hypothesis on $U$.

source.place: Tag 0479 (lemma-make-Jacobson), with an algebraically closed extension of sufficiently large cardinality; the rational-point corollary is used explicitly in Tag 0B8E (spaces-more-groupoids, lemma-group-space-scheme-over-kbar).

proof.text: Choose a set-indexed affine open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in J}\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ a $k$-algebra, using [def-pc-scheme]. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the underlying sets of the $A_i$ to choose an infinite cardinal $\lambda$ strictly larger than $|\coprod_i A_i|$. Thus $|A_i|<\lambda$ for every $i$. By [lem-sfb-algclosed-extension-cardinal-lower-bound], choose an algebraically closed field extension $K/k$ with $\lambda\leq |K|$. This chooses one field for the entire cover, including when $J$ is infinite; for an empty cover the same construction still chooses a field.

source.place: Tag 0479 (lemma-make-Jacobson), first and second proof paragraphs; replace the written maximum by a strict cardinal upper bound on the disjoint union.

proof.text: Let $p:U_K\to U$ be the projection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W=S$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, and rings $R=k$, $A=K$, $B=A_i$. It gives $p^{-1}(V)\cong\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, where $B_i=K\otimes_k A_i$, with its specified $K$-structure. The elements $1\otimes a$, indexed by $a\in A_i$, generate $B_i$ as a $K$-algebra: a pure tensor $c\otimes a$ is $c(1\otimes a)$, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Since $|A_i|<|K|$, [lem-sfb-cardinal-generator-nullstellensatz] makes $B_i$ Jacobson and makes every maximal quotient $B_i/\mathfrak m$ algebraic over $K$.

source.place: Tag 046V (lemma-base-change-Jacobson), proof applying Tag 00FU (theorem-uncountable-nullstellensatz); affine charts are Schemes Tags 01JR and 01I4.

proof.text: The opens $p^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)$ cover $U_K$, since inverse images preserve unions. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-jacobson-spectrum-open-cover] makes each chart a Jacobson topological space, using step 2. Clause (2) of the same node then makes $U_K$ Jacobson. Written out, this is exactly conclusion (i): for any closed subset $Z$ of $U_K$, its intersection with the closed points of $U_K$ is dense in $Z$.

For a closed point $u\in U_K$, choose a chart $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ containing it. The singleton $\{u\}$ remains closed in this open subspace. Under the spectrum description [def-weil-affine-spectrum] it therefore corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$: the closure of a prime $\mathfrak p$ consists of the primes containing $\mathfrak p$, so a closed singleton is maximal. Restricting the structure sheaf to an open leaves its stalk unchanged. By [def-weil-residue-field], $\kappa(u)=(B_i)_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m(B_i)_{\mathfrak m}=B_i/\mathfrak m$: localization does nothing to the field $B_i/\mathfrak m$, because all denominators have nonzero classes. These identifications commute with the structural map from $K$. Thus step 2 makes $\kappa(u)/K$ algebraic.

source.place: Tag 0479 (lemma-make-Jacobson), last proof sentence; the affine residue identification is the local-ring definition.

proof.text: Because $K$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], every nonzero polynomial over $K$ factors into a nonzero constant times linear factors, by successively taking a root and dividing by its linear factor. For $\alpha\in\kappa(u)$ choose a nonzero annihilating polynomial, using step 4. Its degree is positive because the field homomorphism $K\to\kappa(u)$ is injective [def-pc-field-extension]. Evaluating the factorization in the field $\kappa(u)$, one linear factor must vanish, so $\alpha$ is the image of an element of $K$. Thus the structural homomorphism is surjective as well as injective, proving (ii).
